answer: Divergent Path Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed trajectory of nonces; enforcement accepts a new identity only if its first nonce anchors to a prior identity's nadir record, which is unique per lineage and cannot be shared by clones. A clone copying this history collapses onto the same path, so only one branch can bridge to fresh rewards. An attacker splitting N clones therefore pays N distinct histories plus one wasted duplicate lineage each, since any shared ancestry is detected and the whole fork is rejected.
